name: Vitamin E / coconut oil lips

lead: People apply vitamin E oil or coconut oil to their lips for softness and to counter dryness.
Lips lack sweat glands and dry out and chap more easily than other skin.[3]

paras: Oils act as occlusive emollients on the surface. Coconut oil is used in cosmetics and soaps, and its fatty acids appear in cosmetic products.[2]
Wikipedia notes reviews found insufficient evidence for topical vitamin E claims on wound healing and scarring, and allergic contact dermatitis has been reported with tocopheryl derivatives.[1]

lead: Vitamin E and coconut oil are commonly used in home lip care, applied for softness and to ease chapping.

Lips lack sweat glands, so they dry and chap more easily than other skin.[1] Tocopheryl acetate is widely used in skin-care products, but reviews cited by Wikipedia find insufficient evidence for claims about wound healing and scar reduction.[2]
Allergic contact dermatitis from vitamin E derivatives has been reported.[2] Coconut oil is used industrially in cosmetics and soap.[3] No lip-specific trials of either were identified.

paras: Applying vitamin E-containing oil to burns and wounds has a long history, and Wikipedia notes scientific reviews have not supported claims of improved healing, though the belief persists.[2]
Coconut oil is a raw material for soaps and surfactants, and medium-chain fatty acids from it are used in cosmetics.[3]
Allergic contact dermatitis from tocopheryl linoleate and tocopherol acetate in skin-care products has been reported.[2]
